ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, statutory representatives and authorised signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions lists (as transposed into EU law), and the French national asset-freeze measures administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor and TRACFIN. PEP identification and enhanced due diligence are mandatory under Article L.561-10 CMF and applicable AMF/ACPR guidance; a documented risk rating must be applied before any Swift/LC payment rails are activated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: French Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which interfaces with the Registre National des Entreprises and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) / Infogreffe database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in French or any other language using Latin characters, but must be written in a non-misleading and law-abiding form; French transliteration is required for names originally in non-Latin scripts, and the name must be compatible with the principle of clarity and public order; the name of a SAS must not create confusion with an existing RCS-denominated corporate name and may not be identical to a pre-existing protected trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate an independent name-reservation system; priority is established by filing date in the RCS. If the registrar rejects the proposed corporate name, the applicant may (1) file a formal 'recours gracieux' with the same Greffe within 2 months, requesting reversal or substitution of the defective elements; (2) if refused, bring a summary or regular action before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce or the local commercial court within 15 days of the decision; (3) alternatively propose a corrected name variant and refile through the Guichet Unique. No statutory extension of a name reservation is possible; the 30-day window reflects practical planning for a single filing cycle before priority is lost.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial domiciliation company is permissible for administrative registration under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, provided the domiciliation provider is declared and licensed. For a bulk petrochemical/polymer wholesale trader, virtual office is accepted as a legal registered office, but it does not satisfy substantive tax residence or economic-substance requirements; the company must demonstrate effective management and real operational substance in France, in particular for OECD Pillar Two and French CFC/international tax purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Medium (15%) during the first three years of operation; the French tax administration (DGFiP) generally gives notice before an on-site inspection, but customs and anti-fraud agents may conduct unannounced visits under Article L.16B of the French Tax Procedures Code when there is a risk of VAT or customs fraud. The presence of a licensed domiciliation address lowers the risk of ad-hoc physical inspection; however, if the company invoices large quantities of petrochemical goods and uses Swift/LC instruments, enhanced due diligence by its bank may trigger documentary inspections and bank-site verification requests.

incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

At the first meeting of the Board of Directors held on the date of incorporation at the registered office, the following resolutions were adopted unanimously:

1. The share capital has been fully subscribed and paid up by the initial shareholder(s) in the amount of EUR 1 via bank transfer.

2. The registered office is adopted at [full address], and publications in the Journal Officiel are resolved.

3. Mr. [Full Name], born on [date] in [place], residing at [address], is appointed President with full powers for representation and management, including banking operations.

4. Mrs. [Full Name], born on [date] in [place], residing at [address], is appointed Director.

5. Mr. [Full Name], born on [date] in [place], residing at [address], is appointed Secretary.

6. The Board delegates to the President all powers for ordinary and daily management.

7. Compliance with all applicable French laws and regulations is resolved.

This resolution is adopted unanimously on this day.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr; entity incorporation filings are submitted through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; export customs controls and export declaration acceptance are handled by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign shareholder forms the SAS through the Guichet Unique, which transmits the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce. Upon incorporation, the entity is assigned the 9-digit SIREN, a SIRET identifier for each establishment, and is automatically registered for impôt sur les sociétés with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). VAT registration and the intra-Community VAT number are granted by the DGFiP's VIES system upon the taxable activity filing; the French TIN is the SIREN itself and no separate application is required. A non-resident company establishing an SAS must appoint a registered fiscal representative for VAT administration and corporate tax notices where no permanent establishment in France exists; all registration acts are paperless and completed within approximately two to three weeks of the electronic filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows the civil-company legal form under the CGI, and an SAS is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax at entity level. Available statutory elections include: option for VAT consolidation among financially linked enterprises (article 267 C CGI); election of the simplified real VAT regime (régime simplifié) for taxpayers below the statutory turnover ceilings, with annual declaration and quarterly payments; option to report VAT on a cash-receipts basis; exercise of voting rights in the fiscal integration regime (intégration fiscale) under article 223 A CGI for an eligible French parent; and, under the ATAD framework, application of the anti-hybrid neutrality election for controlled transactions under article 209 IX CGI as well as alignment elections for hybrid financial instruments and hybrid permanent establishments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover-based registration threshold for a French-established SAS; any taxable economic activity triggers compulsory VAT registration upon incorporation. For non-established EU sellers, the intra-Community distance-sale and OSS threshold is EUR 10,000 (ex VAT) EU-wide, which is irrelevant to B2B bulk petrochemical wholesale supplies where the customer's valid VAT number supports an intra-Community exemption. The small-business franchise-en-base exemption (EUR 50,000 for goods traders) is not applicable to a wholesale SAS operating in bulk polymer distribution, whose turnover necessarily exceeds the bracket.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing for all domestic B2B transactions under the obligations introduced by the loi de finances pour 2022 and rescheduled by the loi de finances pour 2023. The system operates through the Chorus Pro government platform or approved private dematerialization platforms (Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires – PDP); no per-transaction real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping is applied in France. Invoice data must be transmitted in structured format upon issuance and e-reporting flows are transmitted to the DGFiP periodically; the compulsory e-invoicing sequence begins on 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises, with small and micro enterprises following on 1 January 2027. Invoices issued to foreign customers remain outside the mandatory national clearance channel, and export documentation must nevertheless be retained for the standard six-year tax evidence period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under CGI Articles 262 and 262 ter, a wholesale trader of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules may apply the 0% VAT rate on sales of goods physically dispatched to a third-country destination provided five conditions are cumulatively met: (i) the operation is a transfer of ownership to the purchaser; (ii) the goods are dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the seller or on the seller's behalf within three months of the sale, extendable to six months in limited inward-processing cases; (iii) transport documentation evidences departure from French territory; (iv) the export customs declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation) has been accepted by the DGDDI; and (v) the seller maintains commercial and accounting records demonstrating the physical exit, with the proof retained for six years. Intra-Community supplies to an EU industrial customer are instead exempted under Article 262 ter CGI on condition of the customer's valid French VAT registration status in VIES and the submission of the French recapitulative statement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAU/EAD – Déclaration d'Exportation and its customs release confirmation (visa de la DGDDI) generated through the DELTA-D export system
Transport contract evidencing third-country destination: maritime Bill of Lading (connaissement), CMR road waybill, air waybill, or multimodal transport document
Commercial invoice referencing the export declaration number, the foreign customer's identity, and the Incoterms governing the transfer of dispatch risk
Physical departure proof: customs release statement, container tracking receipt, forwarding instructions, and the carrier's arrival certificate from the destination port
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement receipt evidencing receipt of proceeds in EUR from the foreign buyer within the statutory monetary deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP cross-matches the declarative file against the DGDDI export database (DELTA), French foreign-trade statistics, and the bulk cargo exchange records to verify that zero-rated petrochemical exports physically left the EU within the statutory three-month window. Where the export proof is missing, incomplete, or tardy, the tax authority re-characterizes the zero rating as fully taxable and recovers the unduly exempted VAT with default interest of 0.2% per month (article 1727 CGI), plus a 40% negligence penalty for material omission (article 1728 CGI) or an 80% penalty for deliberate concealment or abuse of law (article 1729 CGI). Fraudulent export zero-rating claims expose the entity and its managers to criminal fines of up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment under article 1741 CGI, exclusion from public procurement, and confiscation of the goods; parallel customs penalties under article 414 of the Code des douanes provide separate imprisonment and fines on the export organizer and the liable customs declarant.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (acting under the European Central Bank / ESCB framework for monetary policy and prudential supervision; Directorate General for Statistics for balance-of-payments reporting)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a Eurozone member, maintains full capital and current account convertibility under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). No FDI screening approval is required for an SAS engaged in wholesale petrochemical trading; non-resident ownership is permitted without prior authorization. Profit remittance to non-EU shareholders is unrestricted, subject to standard corporate distribution documentation (dividend vouchers, board minutes, tax residence certificates) and, where treaty relief is claimed, the appropriate certificate of residence. The euro is legal tender; foreign currency accounts are available for settlement and hedging, but all statistical cross-border flows above Banque de France thresholds (generally EUR 150,000 per financial operation or EUR 75,000 for certain instruments) must be declared electronically via the OFIMA reporting system. There are no exchange controls on the timing of profit repatriation or capital liquidation, and no differentiated FX regime for commodity or petrochemical trading companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirement for export proceeds in France. Eurozone law proscribes any obligation to remit hard-currency receipts to the central bank or to convert export proceeds into euros at a prescribed ratio. However, under the French Monetary and Financial Code and Banque de France regulations, all export receipts (whether denominated in EUR or foreign currency) must be collected through a resident credit institution or approved payment institution and must be declared for balance-of-payments statistical purposes if the transaction value exceeds EUR 12,500 per individual operation or where annual aggregated flows exceed EUR 150,000. Invoices for exports of petrochemical polymers must conform to commercial usance conventions and be settled through documentary instruments (typically irrevocable conformed LCs) or open account within negotiated terms, but no timing limit on retention of foreign currency balances exists and there is no requirement to keep receipts in France beyond standard commercial practice.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary treasury operations, but Low for primary settlement of bulk petrochemical trade. Legal constraints: Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the French E-Money Act may hold funds and route SEPA/ECHF payments, but they are not permitted to take deposits or provide credit and are not official counterparties for irrevocable documentary letters of credit (LCs) or bank guarantees. EMIs are viable for small value disbursements, employee expenses, and FX conversion at low ticket sizes, but for ISIC 4669 wholesale bulk polymer flows requiring multi-million euro wire transfers and shipping-document-backed LCs, a fully licensed French commercial bank or a EU credit institution branch is mandatory. A cross-border overseas EMI with no French passport under PSD2 must be rejected; only EU/EEA EMIs with a branch or passported agent in France are viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated French SAS with non-resident shareholders and a trading-only business,French commercial banks generally require at least one ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and at least one signatory director to attend a live KYC interview in person at a French branch or on a videoconference validated by a notaire/public document verifier. Remote opening is possible for the banking entity as a whole only if the bank accepts a certified digital KYC package (via Labenne, VerifIdentity, or a trust service provider under eIDAS) and the applicant maintains a registered office in France. In practice, most Tier-1 French banks require a physical trip to sign the account agreement and to produce original passport and proof of address, especially when the corporate beneficiary does not have a pre-existing lending relationship. At least one board resolution appointing the signatories, translated into French by a sworn translator, must be physically deposited in case of a full undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO jurisdiction in a non-EU grey listed jurisdiction or tax haven
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract of ultimate shareholders, notarized chain-of-title for each beneficiary, FATCA/CRS self-certification, tax residence certificates, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose for the non-EU entity holding shares (e.g., family holding or investment vehicle). French banks additionally require a negative OECD/IFU screening and proof of source of wealth for UBOs (e.g., audited financial statements, inheritance or tax receipts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity for bulk petrochemical polymers without immediate physical logistics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide signed term-sales contracts (ensuing from ISIC 4669 wholesale), master supply agreements, pro forma invoices, confirming the commercial substance of each wire; freight and shipping evidence (bills of lading, packing lists, quality inspection certificates from SGS/BV or equivalent), warehouse receipts if goods are resold from bonded storage, and a 12-month treasury forecast with recurring counterparties to demonstrate that the transaction pattern matches a genuine wholesale trading operation rather than a pass-through laundering structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or signatories lacking prior banking history in France
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalized passport color scans, notarized apostilled power of attorney if a mandated signatory is appointed, certified diploma or professional reference letters to evidence experience in international commodity trading, a detailed corporate registry extract (including KBIS for the SAS in France), and a signed

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Importance of public funding / state aid or politically exposed person (PEP) links in the supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive PEP declaration signed by all UBOs and directors, a beneficial ownership register (papiers in French) filed with the French Ministry of Justice, and a PEP waiver or compliance letter from the bank's sanctions department confirming that the PEP link is passive and does not conflict with French/European sanctions regimes. For producers in sanctioned jurisdictions, obtain a general authorization from the EU competent authority and a written independent legal opinion confirming end-use legality.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an SAS, capital contributions are paid by wire into a recipient bank account in France. The transfer from a non-EU shareholder must be executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (if no beneficiary details required) with the exact purpose listing 'Additional paid-in capital / Capital injection for wholesale petrochemical trading activity under ISIC 4669'. French banks will treat the inflow as a financial operation and require the receiving institution to obtain a copy of the corporate resolution of the shareholders, the bank account statement showing the credit, and confirmation that the contribution does not originate from shell-company veil breaches. If the capital is injected as shareholder advance (compte courant d'associé), the routing must be labeled 'Loan agreement between SAS and shareholder dated DD/MM/YYYY' to avoid recharacterization as taxable income. For capital transfers exceeding EUR 150,000 in a calendar month, the bank will submit an OFIMA declaration to the Banque de France. The receiving French bank must be provided with the beneficiary ISIN/LEI and the sworn translation of the French articles of association to validate the account ownership.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for bulk polymer purchases from suppliers in non-EU jurisdictions are cleared through (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account payments, (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit (LC) issued under ICC UCP 600 (and related eUCP rules) in European banks, typically with confirmation added by a global bank in the supplier's country, and (iii) documentary collections (DP/DA) under ICC URC 522 for more sensitive counterparties. For high-value transborder flows, the French paying bank is required to report the transaction to the Banque de France under the balance-of-payments regime and may require an advance declaration if the operation equals or exceeds EUR 150,000 or where the counterparty is located in a third country. A recommended structure for this ISIC 4669 scope is a framework Standby LC issued in favour of top-tier polymer suppliers (e.g., in the Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, USA, or Qatar), coupled with MT103 wires against delivery. For Chinese or Southeast Asian suppliers, a usance LC with a sight confirmation fee is preferred to guarantee the timing of title transfer. All outbound disbursements must be matched to a pro forma invoice or purchase contract and accompanied by an end-use certificate where the porphyria of polymer grades is subject to strategic end-use controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts (rollable up to 24 months)
EUR/CNY deliverable forward contracts for invoices originating in Chinese renminbi
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF forwards for European cross-currency settlements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies such as INR, IDR, BRL, TRY and VND where the underlying receivable is in a non-convertible or non-deliverable currency
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) to hedge long-term procurement or financing exposures
FX swaps to manage temporary mismatches between euro receipts and foreign-currency trade payables
FX options (vanilla and exotic) with short-term maturity up to 36 months, only for plain-vanilla hedging of a known underlying transaction exposure
Currency collars and participating forwards for protection against adverse moves while retaining upside flexibility on commodity trade payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (bilan, compte de résultat, annexes) with the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval of accounts; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year end. For a calendar-year SAS, accounts are due by 31 July (approval by 30 June, deposit by 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit exposes the legal representative to a fine up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 4,500 for legal entities). The court may issue an injunctive order with mandatory penalty payment (astreinte) per day of non-compliance; repeated failure can lead to court-ordered appointment of a special agent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale – form 2065 and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December: no later than the third business day after 1 May (typically 3 May). For off-calendar year ends: the third business day following the 30th day after fiscal year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 5% delinquency surcharge on the unpaid income tax, increasing to 10% if not filed within 30 days of a formal notice, plus monthly interest at 0.2%. If no corporate tax is due, a flat penalty of EUR 150 applies for failure to respond to a filing request.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business premises declaration (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – form 1447-C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 1 September for the following year; or within 30 days of a change in business premises or cessation of activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted declaration results in a 10% annual surcharge on the assessed tax, plus 0.2% monthly interest; understatement can trigger an additional 50% penalty for insufficiency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a French SAS when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded as of the fiscal year end: total assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average permanent employees exceeding 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) as mandated by Article L123-13 of the French Commercial Code; IFRS applies only for consolidated financial statements of listed (or exceptional) groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual beneficial ownership re-declaration in France. The SAS is required to file an updated Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs (DBE) with the Court Registry within 30 days of any share transfer that changes direct or indirect ownership. At the annual filing of accounts, the Registry cross-check makes it a practical duty to confirm that the DBE remains current; failure to update exposes the company to a fine up to EUR 1,000 per company and up to EUR 500 per director.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholder Decisions (Registre des décisions d'associés)
Share Transfer Register (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Minutes of General Meetings (Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% standard corporate income tax rate; top effective rate approximately 25.8% including the 3.3% social contribution on tax payable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and at least 75% owned by individuals). Participation exemption regime normally yields 95% tax exemption on qualifying dividend income. French tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but annual utilisation is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding that amount; carryback of losses is permitted for three years up to EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultats) together with annexes 2052 through 2059-SD, filed electronically through the EFI/ERD portal managed by DGFiP (télé-IRIS or EDI partner software).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; four mandatory corporate income tax prepayments are due quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the balance paid upon filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December: second business day after 1 May. For a fiscal year ending on any other date: within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat fiscal: net taxable profit or loss before carryforwards and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident SAS has no French permanent establishment, report zero; if a French PE is recognised, allocate only the French-source trading profit attributable to that PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déficits reportables en avant: French tax loss carryforwards applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only French losses; annual deduction is subject to the EUR 1,000,000 + 50% excess cap. Foreign losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Plus-values et moins-values nettes à long terme: net long-term capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Long-term capital gains benefit from a reduced 33.33% fraction in the CIT computation; non-residents with a French PE must include gains from disposal of French business assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Crédits et réductions d'impôt: available tax credits such as the research credit, apprenticeship tax credit and other recoverable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to credits genuinely linked to the French PE activity; a wholesale petrochemical trading SAS will generally claim none.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Siège du contrôle ou de direction: declaration of place of effective management for tax residence purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm whether effective management and control are in France; if the place of effective management is in another jurisdiction, ensure treaty residence remittance is considered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenue à la source sur les produits distribués: dividend and deemed-dividend withholding tax declaration for distributions to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French paying company must file this box together with Form 2561/2561-B and remit 30% withholding tax unless treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase in corporate tax due; if the return remains unfiled 30 days after a formal notice (mise en demeure), the surcharge is 40%; deliberate concealment or fraud attracts an 80% surcharge. Late payment is separately charged monthly interest at 0.2% of the outstanding tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% on gross French-source dividends paid by an SAS to non-residents; reduced to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (generally requiring a direct holding of at least 10%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate or the 0% parent-subsidiary exemption, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) issued by its home-state tax authority, together with the French administrative Form 5000/5001 (or applicable equivalent), to the French paying company before the distribution date. The paying company must retain these documents and may apply the reduced rate at source. If tax was withheld at the domestic rate, a refund claim must be filed with the local DGFiP service before the statutory limitation deadline; the EU interest/dividends/royalty Directive also provides a rapid refund mechanism for EU parent companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, trademarks, know-how and similar IP paid by a French SAS to non-residents carry a statutory withholding tax of 33.33%; most French tax treaties reduce this to a 0%–10% domestic treaty rate. Interest on ordinary cross-border commercial debt is generally exempt from French statutory withholding tax, and most DTA provisions also cap or eliminate French taxing rights; interest that is recharacterised as hidden equity distribution may nonetheless be treated as a dividend and taxed at 30%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 in annual gross revenue or total gross balance-sheet assets for the local entity; the Master File/CbCR reporting threshold is set at EUR 750,000,000 for the consolidated group turnover.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations certificate system, but applies the OECD substance-over-form standard: an SAS used as a shell or letterbox without real local employees, physical assets, management decisions or commercial activity will be denied treaty benefits under the MLI Principal Purpose Test and may be recharacterised under the French GAAR (abus de droit). A wholly artificial structure cannot enjoy reduced WHT, participation exemptions or foreign tax credit benefits, and risks treatment as a taxable sham with retrospective reassessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating French corporate income, issuing fictitious invoices for petrochemical purchases or resales, concealing trading profits held through undisclosed nominees, or failing to file the SAS income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic penalty of 80% of evaded tax plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.2%; criminal court penalty under Article 1741 CGI of five years' imprisonment, a fine of up to EUR 1,050,000 (increased to seven years for aggravated offences) plus publication and confiscation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director, chairman and de facto directors may be prosecuted personally even where the company is the formal taxable entity; directors can be ordered to pay all evaded taxes, interest and penalties jointly with the company under Article L.267 LPF, and may suffer a travel ban, asset freezing order and prohibition from managing a commercial undertaking.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reselling virgin PE and PP granules to or from related trading companies at non-arm's-length margins, making round-trip transactions through intermediary entities in low-tax or non-transparent jurisdictions, or failing to produce local and master file documentation upon DGFiP request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment substituting an arm's-length profit, with taxation of the difference, late-payment interest and a 40% penalty for inadequate documentation; a fixed fine of EUR 10,000 may also be imposed for failure to surrender TP documentation; double tax exposure is mitigated through mutual agreement procedures and MAP arbitration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly set or approved artificial intercompany margins can be held jointly and severally liable for the additional corporate tax and penalties; serious manipulation evidence may support criminal fraud charges and lead to travel bans, professional disqualification and confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SAS exclusively as a booking vehicle with no local staff, no management activity in France, nominal capital, contracts executed offshore, and beneficial owners based in tax havens; distributing dividends to an EU parent lacking substance solely to claim the 0% Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA and EU directive relief, retroactive reassessment at the 30% withholding tax rate, GAAR penalty of 80% where artifice is proved, and extension of the regular three-year statute of limitations to ten years; foreign intermediary structures may be struck down under the abuse of law procedure (article L.64 LPF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominal directors and actual beneficiaries risk joint civil liability for all withholding taxes, penalties and interest; travel restrictions, temporary interdiction to manage companies and, in egregious fraud cases, imprisonment for tax evasion or money laundering are applicable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Settling polymer import transactions through shell payment agents, unreported cash deposits, false bills of lading, counterparty sanctions evasions, or incomplete beneficial-owner declarations on the SAS within French corporate registries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French criminal penalties for money laundering (Code monétaire et financier, art. L.465-1) for corporate entities can reach EUR 5,000,000 or five times the value of laundered funds, while individuals face five years' imprisonment and fines up to EUR 375,000; administrative sanctions and licence withdrawal may also be applied by ACPR/TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge of or negligence contributing to money laundering can be prosecuted personally, with civil restitution orders, freezing of bank accounts, passport seizure, travel bans, prohibition from holding board positions, and, for serious breaches, imprisonment before the case is remitted to the public prosecutor; the corporate veil is pierced in respect of deliberately obscured cash flows and undisclosed beneficial owners.
